Troubleshooting Pipeline Data Mismatches: Reconciliation & Drift

11 min read Updated: November 2026 By Rajvardhan Singh Rathore
When financial billing dashboards disagree with operational warehouse reports, supply chain operations stall. Learn how to systematically diagnose, isolate, and remediate data pipeline mismatches.

Anatomy of a Freight Data Discrepancy

Data discrepancies in logistics architectures typically stem from one of three flaws:

  • Late-Arriving Accessorial Charges: Carrier invoices include detention, fuel surcharge, or liftgate fees received weeks after delivery.
  • Timezone Normalization Disconnect: Billing runs on Eastern Time (US/Eastern) while warehouse scans are recorded in UTC, shifting cutoffs.
  • Dimensional Re-Weigh Discrepancy: Carrier high-speed sorting scales re-weigh packages and invoice based on dimensional weight rather than declared weight.

The 4-Step Discrepancy Isolation Method

  1. Identify the discrepancy boundary: Compare row counts and numerical sums at daily intervals.
  2. Isolate affected carrier partitions: Determine if the defect is systemic or confined to a specific carrier SCAC.
  3. Inspect raw audit payloads: Verify if the raw carrier JSON or EDI file matched the transformed warehouse values.
  4. Deploy targeted backfill: Apply idempotent update script across affected shipment partitions.

Diagnostic Reconciliation SQL Script

PostgreSQL Discrepancy Audit SQL 
SELECT 
  o.shipment_id,
  o.declared_charge_usd AS erp_expected_charge,
  i.invoiced_charge_usd AS carrier_invoiced_charge,
  (i.invoiced_charge_usd - o.declared_charge_usd) AS variance_usd,
  ROUND(((i.invoiced_charge_usd - o.declared_charge_usd) / NULLIF(o.declared_charge_usd, 0) * 100)::numeric, 2) AS variance_pct,
  i.carrier_accessorial_notes
FROM erp_shipment_orders o
JOIN carrier_freight_invoices i ON o.tracking_number = i.tracking_number
WHERE ABS(i.invoiced_charge_usd - o.declared_charge_usd) > 5.00
ORDER BY variance_usd DESC;
